issue.title: feat: Support quad+ backticks for nested markdown codeblocks
issue.body:
## Problem

When trying to save files that contain markdown codeblocks (like documentation with code examples), the inner triple backticks close the outer save block prematurely.

## Example

Trying to save a markdown file with embedded code blocks:

````save /path/to/file.md
# Example Doc

```python
print('hello')
```
````

The inner ```python``` closes the outer save block.

## Current Behavior

The codeblock parser in `gptme/codeblock.py` uses:
```python
re_triple_tick_start = re.compile(r"^```.*\n")
re_triple_tick_end = re.compile(r"^```$")
```

This only matches exactly triple backticks.

## Expected Behavior

Support quad (or more) backticks as outer delimiters, where inner triple backticks are preserved. This is standard CommonMark behavior.

## Workaround

Use language tags on inner "lang-less" codeblocks (e.g., ```tree instead of just ```) so they aren't detected as closing the outer block.

## References

- CommonMark spec allows 3+ backticks, with outer fence needing more than inner
- GitHub Flavored Markdown supports this

steps:
Save a markdown file docs/example.md whose exact content is:

# Example Doc

```python
print('hello')
```
expected: docs/example.md is written with the heading and the complete fenced python block (an outer fence of four or more backticks keeps the inner triple backticks).
defect: The inner ```python block closes the outer save block prematurely, so the saved file is truncated.
Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/gptme/gptme/pull/1009 (commit fe24f45cbc4276815818ab13c5f6c6b1cfa6ddbf). gptme's markdown tool format extracts tool calls with _extract_codeblocks() in gptme/codeblock.py, which recognised only fences starting with exactly ``` and used `line.startswith("```")` / `line.strip() == "```"` to open and close blocks, so a ````save block was not tracked by its fence length and the first inner bare ``` closed it. PR #1009 records the opening fence length (3+ backticks) and only closes the block on a bare fence of the same length, per CommonMark. Ships in v0.32.0; the pinned revision contains it.
